item.title: Some fishers lure sharks into shallow waters, causing concern in New Jersey
item.description: Shark fishing videos caused concern this summer in New Jersey, as some people lured big sharks close to swimmers. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Farm linked to cyclosporaisis outbreak went years without FDA inspection
item.description: The FDA has long fallen short of legally required inspection targets, and foreign inspections fell further last year amid agency layoffs.

item.title: In texts, Fauci discussed potential risks, benefits of COVID vaccine for pregnant women
item.description: Two Senate Republicans released a set of 2021 texts that show Dr. Anthony Fauci discussing how to "weigh the potential risks against the benefits" of pregnant women taking COVID-19 vaccines.

item.title: Doctor discusses released Fauci texts on the COVID vaccine and pregnant women
item.description: Republican senators this week released 11 new text messages from Dr. Anthony Fauci's government phone in 2021 as part of the investigations into his handling of the COVID pandemic. In the texts, he discussed the potential risks and benefits of the vaccine for pregnant women. Dr. Serena Chen, an OB-GYN and the director of advocacy at CCRM Fertility of New Jersey, has more.

item.title: Rescuers race to find Colombia earthquake survivors as death toll rises
item.description: Over 1,100 homes were destroyed when Colombia was struck by its strongest earthquake on record.

item.title: Colombia reels from worst earthquake on record: "It felt like it'd never end"
item.description: The worst earthquake on record hit Colombia on Monday, measuring a magnitude of 7.4. Colombia's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said at least 181 people are dead, with hundreds more missing. Lilia Luciano reports from Colombia.

item.title: Powerful storms slam Midwest, leave nearly 1 million without power
item.description: Nearly 1 million customers in the Midwest were without power as perilous thunderstorms and extreme wind gusts pummeled the region on Tuesday.

item.title: Thunderstorms cause major travel delays, ground stops
item.description: Storms in the Midwest caused widespread travel troubles on Tuesday. More than 7,000 flights were delayed or canceled, with the biggest backlogs in Chicago and New York. Kris Van Cleave reports from Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Trump secretly switched to different plane in Turkey amid Iran threat
item.description: Ahead of a flight from Turkey, President Trump secretly left Air Force One and was moved to another plane with the help of a catering truck, according to a source, as the U.S. grappled with a threat from Iran.

item.title: What's at stake as voters cast ballots in six primaries, including South Carolina and Wisconsin
item.description: Primary elections are being held Tuesday in six states: Wisconsin, Minnesota, Alabama, Connecticut, Vermont and South Carolina. CBS News' Taurean Small, Jonah Kaplan, Mark Strassmann and Anthony Salvanto have the latest.

item.title: Storms hit Midwest as wildfires rage in western states
item.description: Powerful storms swept across the Midwest and into the mid-Atlantic states on Tuesday night. The outbreak of storms brought hurricane-force winds of up to 100 miles per hour, along with tornadoes and flash flooding. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Trump took secret flight from Turkey NATO summit last month due to Iranian missile threat
item.description: President Trump secretly switched from Air Force One to a different plane after a NATO summit in Turkey last month. The U.S. had learned of a credible Iranian missile threat as he left Turkey's capital. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: FDA last inspected Mexican farm linked to cyclospora outbreak in 2019, records show
item.description: CBS News has learned that the Mexican lettuce farm connected to the outbreak of a nasty intestinal illness hasn't been inspected by American regulators in more than seven years. Food safety advocates blame budget and personnel cuts for a 29% drop in inspection rates of foreign farms over the past two years.

item.title: U.S. military operations killed 153 civilians last year, Pentagon says
item.description: The Pentagon has acknowledged that U.S. military operations killed more than 150 civilians in 2025. The count did not include any deaths from airstrikes on boats in the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean.

item.title: New forecast shifts GOP Rep. Max Miller's reelection race to "toss-up"
item.description: As scandal-plagued Republican Rep. Max Miller of Ohio continues his reelection bid, political forecaster Sabato's Crystal Ball says the race has moved toward the Democrats and is now a toss-up. Wall Street Journal politics reporter Sabrina Rodriguez and NOTUS senior editor Dave Levinthal join to discuss.

item.title: Transportation Secretary Duffy discusses new technology aimed at making air travel safer
item.description: Top transportation officials were at Newark Airport on Tuesday for the installation of a new radar system designed to help controllers prevent runway incidents. CBS News senior transportation correspondent Kris Van Cleave spoke with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy about the new technology.

item.title: White House asked DOJ about new Reflecting Pool case against David Hearn
item.description: Earlier this month, however, federal prosecutors moved to dismiss the case, citing new information that the damage was caused by a "botched installation" by a contractor, not vandalism.

item.title: Trump administration bars use of Medicaid funds for some youth transgender care
item.description: Medicaid said it won't pay for gender-affirming surgeries or hormones for transgender minors.

item.title: Trump Media sells $100,000 Truth Social data access, drawing scrutiny
item.description: Customers are paying up to $100,000 a month for faster access to Truth Social posts from President Trump and other top users of the social media platform.

item.title: Rep. Meng slams DOJ memo extending executive privilege to outside advisers
item.description: A new Justice Department memo says President Trump can assert executive privilege with so-called "private advisers." These protections historically have been limited to executive branch employees. Democratic Rep. Grace Meng of New York, who sits on the House Appropriations Committee, joins "The Takeout" with her reaction.

item.title: High school football player finds venomous snake inside helmet he was wearing
item.description: The Maumelle High football player wore the helmet for nearly an hour and was fortunate he wasn't bitten, animal services director Chris Davis said.

item.title: Details on Trump's secret Air Force One swap over Iranian threat
item.description: The Washington Post reports that in July, President Trump dodged an Iranian threat in Turkey by sneaking off Air Force One and into an aviation catering container which brought him to another plane. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe has the details. Then, Marine Corps veteran and former CIA officer Elliot Ackerman joins with analysis.

item.title: On the ground in South Carolina, Wisconsin and Minnesota as primaries near end
item.description: Tuesday's primary races in Wisconsin and Minnesota will provide clues about democratic socialist momentum. Meanwhile, the South Carolina primary will shed light on the MAGA mindset in one of the earliest states to attach itself to President Trump. CBS News' Mark Strassmann, Taurean Small and Jonah Kaplan have the latest from across the three states.

item.title: California high-speed rail could run out of money by December 2027, as authority cuts train order in half
item.description: The watchdog's review warns the $4 billion federal funding loss now leaves the project needing billions in financing within 16 months — as the rail authority acknowledges for the first time that it still has no train contract, has cut its order from six trains to three, and has dropped the "Buy America" requirement.

item.title: Play video games? You, too, could become an air traffic controller
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is touting the success of a campaign targeting video gamers to train as air traffic controllers.

item.title: What's behind the $4B funding cut for California's high-speed rail?
item.description: Records reveal California twice missed deadlines to buy the trains at the center of a federal funding fight — then quietly dropped its lawsuit weeks after missing its new deadline.

item.title: Measles outbreak "slowing," but newborn's family still can't meet her
item.description: Utah's weekly measles case count has fallen. The national tally hasn't, and a newborn who's too young to be vaccinated is caught in between.

item.title: The anatomy of a big chief showdown
item.description: In the Mardi Gras Indian, or Black Masking Indian, tradition, the big chiefs and their crews — spy boys, flag boys, wild men and a big queen — square off in mock battles with other so-called tribes to determine who is, in their words, the "prettiest."

item.title: Veteran faces childhood trauma on psychedelic journey
item.description: Navy veteran Michael Giardina told Anderson Cooper he was able to "let go" of trauma from his childhood during a psychedelic experience.

item.title: What inspired the outfits in "The Handmaid's Tale"
item.description: In an interview with 60 Minutes correspondent Jon Wertheim, author Margaret Atwood joked about the signature red cloak and bonnet: "Well, if you have a cult, and if you have totalitarianism, you have to have outfits."
